title: Conscience
definition: Conscience is the God-given inner witness that bears moral awareness, though it must be trained and corrected by Scripture.
summary: The conscience can accuse or excuse, but it must be shaped by God's truth.
christFocus: Jesus cleanses the conscience through His blood and leads believers into sincere faith and obedience.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The conscience is part of God's moral design in humanity. It can accuse, excuse, warn, or approve. Yet because of sin, the conscience can be weak, wounded, misinformed, hardened, or defiled.

For this reason, conscience is not the final authority. It must be shaped by Scripture and submitted to God. A person can feel peace and still be wrong, or feel guilt over something Scripture does not forbid.

Christ cleanses the conscience through His saving work. Believers are called to pursue a clear conscience before God and others, walking in love and truth.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people are ruled either by false guilt or by a hardened conscience that no longer responds to sin. Conscience matters because it teaches believers to let Scripture, not feelings alone, train moral judgment.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your conscience under the Word of God. Confess real sin, reject false guilt, avoid wounding the conscience of others, and seek to live honestly before the Lord.
